name: Springfield quick-frozen food retail
description: Birds Eye quick-frozen foods reached retail shoppers in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1930; the company introduced an inexpensive rental display case later, in 1934.

date.basis: Date refers to the scoped documented case, not global origin.

events.statement: Birds Eye quick-frozen foods reached retail shoppers in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1930; the company introduced an inexpensive rental display case later, in 1934.

evidence.supports: The institutional account describes Birdseye’s quick-freezing work and the 1930 Springfield retail introduction. It describes leased cases but does not date their introduction.
The business history places the Springfield introduction in 1930 and the rental case program in 1934, after earlier expensive display cases and financing arrangements.

events.caveats: Freezing foods was older and practiced by Indigenous communities; this is one commercial retail introduction, not the invention of freezing. Rental cases are a later development, not a dated feature of the 1930 launch.

evidence.supports: The institutional account credits Birdseye with development of the quick-freezing technology behind the Springfield introduction; it does not date the later lease program.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of this documented case, not a claim of global first.
